backlog.title: How to Support Scorpio Without Pushing
backlog.hook: When Scorpio goes quiet in a rough patch, more questions can feel like more pressure.
backlog.angle: Scorpio | Single AI host | Use a friendship situation: one person wants to help, but repeated questions make the quiet friend withdraw further. Contrast one steady check-in with demanding an immediate explanation. Keep the counter-view explicit: space is not permission to disappear indefinitely.

backlog.title: What Libra Actually Calls Romantic
backlog.hook: Libra notices the tiny detail you remembered more than the expensive date you planned.

backlog.title: Libra Has an Opinion—They Are Reading the Room
backlog.hook: Libra does have an opinion. They just want to know it is safe to say it.
backlog.angle: Libra | Single AI host | Start with the difference between having no opinion and checking whether disagreement will be punished. Use a partner asking what Libra really thinks, then calling the answer mean or dramatic. Keep this as a relationship behavior pattern, not a universal rule.
backlog.why_now: checked_at=2026-08-21; research topic miraa-w34-mix21-t03 is supported by verified source src-3243021320, a directly readable Libra Reddit thread whose comments repeatedly ask for quality time and room to have strong opinions without being called mean; visible comment scores include 40, 19 and 15. Dedupe: this is not the existing dinner-choice conflict; the single test variable is whether disagreement feels safe.
backlog.route_reason: Evergreen Route C; one host can show the opinion-versus-safety contrast while keeping the current single-host test baseline.

backlog.title: When Cancer Stops Being the Family Fixer
backlog.hook: Cancer can love the family and still refuse to carry every family problem.
backlog.angle: Cancer | Single AI host | Use one family-group-chat problem that everyone expects Cancer to solve. Show the boundary as a specific refusal to take one more task, not as cutting the family off. Avoid diagnosis, inherited-trauma claims or treating caregiving as destiny.
